questions.prompt: I cannot bear this burden alone, I entreat you, uncle.
questions.answer: Hoc onus sōlus ferre nequeō, quaesō, patrue.

questions.prompt: We entreat the gods, since we are unable to escape the danger.
questions.answer: Deōs quaesumus, cum perīculum effugere nequeāmus.

questions.prompt: The soldier, wounded in the throat, cannot speak.
questions.answer: Mīles, in iugulō vulnerātus, loquī nequit.

questions.prompt: Give me the sword, for I entreat you to defend the city.
questions.answer: Cedo gladium, nam tē quaesō ut urbem dēfendās.

questions.prompt: Hail, guardian of the city, who wards off dangers from us!
questions.answer: Salvē, urbis vindex, quī perīcula ā nōbīs prohibēs!

questions.prompt: Hail, friends, you who have returned unharmed from war!
questions.answer: Salvēte, amīcī, quī ex bellō incolumēs redīstis!

questions.prompt: He bade his uncle good day with a cheerful voice.
questions.answer: Patruum vōce hilarī salvēre iussit.

questions.prompt: Hail, Caesar; we who are about to die salute you.
questions.answer: Havē, Caesar, moritūrī tē salūtāmus.

questions.prompt: If you can, tell me by what reward virtue is nourished.
questions.answer: Sī quīs, cedo quō praemiō virtūs alātur.

questions.prompt: We can define the word, but we cannot explain its origin.
questions.answer: Vocābulum dēfinīre quīmus, sed orīginem eius explicāre nequīmus.

questions.prompt: They cannot come to their senses, though the danger hangs over them.
questions.answer: Resipīscere nequeunt, quamquam perīculum eīs impendet.

questions.prompt: Give me those letters, please; I entreat you.
questions.answer: Cette illās litterās, quaesō.

questions.prompt: Since the juice flows from the wounded tree, we cannot save it.
questions.answer: Cum sūcus ex arbore vulnerātā fluat, eam servāre nequīmus.

questions.prompt: I entreat you all: point out to me the straight path.
questions.answer: Vōs omnēs quaesō: mōnstrāte mihi viam rēctam.

questions.prompt: Hail, avenger, you upon whom our safety depends!
questions.answer: Salvē, vindex, ā quō salūs nostra pendet!

questions.prompt: We entreat you, uncle, to hand over the promised reward.
questions.answer: Tē quaesumus, patrue, ut praemium prōmissum trādās.

questions.prompt: Tell me the name by which this remedy is defined.
questions.answer: Cedo nōmen quō hoc remedium dēfinītur.

questions.prompt: Although he had recovered his senses, he could not stand up.
questions.answer: Quamquam resipuerat, surgere nequībat.

questions.prompt: Hail, you who have succeeded to your father's kingdom!
questions.answer: Salvē, quī in patris rēgnum successistī!

questions.prompt: We entreat the judge lest an innocent man be condemned through a fault.
questions.answer: Iūdicem quaesumus nē innocēns vitiō damnētur.

questions.prompt: Hail, friend! Give me your hand, I entreat you.
questions.answer: Salvē, amīce! Cedo mihi manum, quaesō.

questions.prompt: Those who cling to vice cannot be praised.
questions.answer: Quī vitiō adhaerent laudārī nequeunt.

questions.prompt: We can find no one unlike him in courage.
questions.answer: Nēminem virtūte eī dissimilem reperīre quīmus.
